nodes.author: Elhoushi, Shrivastava, Liskovich, Hosmer, Basti, Wasti, Lai, et al.
nodes.rationale: Make early exits accurate at training time with layer dropout + an early-exit loss where all layers share the same exit; 1.34–2.16× speedups (2.16× CNN/DM, 1.82× code, 2.0× TOPv2), plus self-speculative decoding.

nodes.label: Think-at-Hard (TaH) arXiv 2511.08577 (Fu, You, Chen, Dai, Yang, Wang)
nodes.author: Fu, You, Chen, Dai, Yang, Wang
nodes.norm_label: think-at-hard (tah) arxiv 2511.08577 (fu, you, chen, dai, yang, wang)
nodes.rationale: Fine-tunes Qwen3-Base 0.6B and 1.7B. On Ouro-1.7B the oracle iteration policy 'iterates on 12–19% of tokens' and improves downstream performance by 2.0–7.3%; the shipped decider skips 93% of tokens while beating always-iterate by 3.8–4.4%. Two-stage: imitation of a static oracle policy + depth-aware LoRA applied ONLY at iterations d > 1 so the first-pass prediction is preserved.

nodes.label: Huginn — Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning arXiv 2502.05171 (Geiping et al., 3.5B / 800B tokens)
nodes.author: Geiping, McLeish, Jain, Kirchenbauer, Singh, Bartoldson, Kailkhura, Bhatele, Goldstein
nodes.norm_label: huginn — scaling up test-time compute with latent reasoning arxiv 2502.05171 (geiping et al., 3.5b / 800b tokens)
nodes.rationale: Log-normal-Poisson loop count (r̄=32, σ=0.5), backprop through last k=8 iterations, L(θ)=E_x E_r L(m_θ(x,r),x') — loss at the sampled depth, no depth mixture, no halting weights. Fig 6: val ppl at depths 1,4,8,16,32,64 all improve during training.

nodes.label: Huang et al. 2016 — Deep Networks with Stochastic Depth arXiv 1603.09382
nodes.author: Huang, Sun, Liu, Sedra, Weinberger
nodes.norm_label: huang et al. 2016 — deep networks with stochastic depth arxiv 1603.09382
nodes.rationale: Origin of stochastic depth. >1200 layers, 4.91% CIFAR-10 error vs 5.25%/6.41% constant-depth ResNets. Read also as an implicit ensemble of 2^L subnetworks.

nodes.label: LoopFormer arXiv 2602.11451 (Jedi, Ciccone, Taati)
nodes.author: Jedi, Ciccone, Taati
nodes.rationale: Every batch runs the full L-loop trajectory AND a sampled shortcut S~U{1..L−1}; L = L_L + 0.1·L_S + 0.1·L_cons. Each loop conditioned on normalized time t and step size Δ. Recipe cost ≈ C(L)+E[C(M)] ≈ 1.5× the fixed-depth step. Looped models trail non-looped on ppl; step schedule matters (larger steps early, finer late; PPL spread across schedules up to ~3).

nodes.label: CALM — Confident Adaptive Language Modeling, Schuster et al. 2022 arXiv 2207.07061 (NeurIPS 2022 oral)
nodes.author: Schuster, Fisch, Gupta, Dehghani, Bahri, Tran, Tay, Metzler
nodes.norm_label: calm — confident adaptive language modeling, schuster et al. 2022 arxiv 2207.07061 (neurips 2022 oral)
nodes.rationale: T5-1.1 8-layer, code in t5x. Exit when c_t^i ≥ λ_t^i. Up to 3× speedup with provable consistency; the ORACLE bound is 5.2×. Shares the output embedding and ONE early-exit classifier across all layers — no per-layer heads. The winning criterion is the softmax RESPONSE (margin), not top-1 probability.

nodes.norm_label: recurtrace arxiv 2609.03379 (wang, feng, shen, xu, wang, wu; 1.7b, mathqa, 2400 items)

nodes.label: Byte models lose at small compute, close at scale, win on robustness
nodes.norm_label: byte models lose at small compute, close at scale, win on robustness
nodes.rationale: ByT5 (2105.13626), bGPT 110M (2402.19155), BLT matching Llama-3-style BPE up to 8B/4T bytes with better long-tail robustness (2412.09871). Patching strategy decides everything at small scale: SpaceByte's dynamic boundary rule beats fixed-size patching (2404.14408); H-Net needs >1B params for one stage (2507.07955); MegaByte is the floor not the ceiling (2305.07185).

nodes.label: Data filtering is the largest documented lever at fixed compute
nodes.norm_label: data filtering is the largest documented lever at fixed compute
nodes.rationale: DCLM produced a 7B model at 64% MMLU 5-shot, +6.6pp over the previous open-data SOTA with 40% less compute (arXiv:2406.11794); FineWeb-Edu moved a 1.71B model from 33% to 37% MMLU and 46% to 57% ARC (arXiv:2406.17557); SmolLM2 confirms the same ordering below 1B (arXiv:2502.02737). Dormouse: the corpus was ~44 GB raw with no documented dedup or quality filtering.

nodes.label: What to DELETE: halt head, KoLeo, output-side lookup, expert-choice, warmup, MSA at s512
nodes.norm_label: what to delete: halt head, koleo, output-side lookup, expert-choice, warmup, msa at s512
nodes.rationale: Each deletion carries its citation: 2608.22347 for the halt head, 2304.07193 for KoLeo, 2501.16975 for output-side tables, 2409.02060 for expert-choice, the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next report for batch warmup (-18.8% extra steps, no gain), 2502.11089 for MSA at s512 (at 512 bytes the quadratic term being sparsified is a rounding error), 2411.04330 for sub-4-bit and fp8-forward-by-default on long runs. TSCT is demoted to a matched-param A/B.

nodes.label: EBT energy head: InfoNCE over candidates, strongest scaling evidence
nodes.norm_label: ebt energy head: infonce over candidates, strongest scaling evidence
nodes.rationale: Contrastive energy head over (context, candidate) pairs; ~35% faster scaling w.r.t. data/depth/params/FLOPs and +29% more gain from extra inference compute than Transformer++ (arXiv:2507.02092).

nodes.label: Fine-grained token-choice MoE, no shared expert
nodes.norm_label: fine-grained token-choice moe, no shared expert
nodes.rationale: OLMoE's controlled sweeps: 64 small experts with 8 routed beats 8 experts with 8 routed; token-choice beats expert-choice at matched budget; a shared expert did not help and can hurt. Matches dense 7B quality with under half the training FLOPs (arXiv:2409.02060). Caveat: OLMoE pays in total-parameter memory, exactly the resource dormouse is short on.

nodes.label: Hybrid linear:full attention converges near 3:1
nodes.rationale: Three independent 2025 results agree on the ratio, not just the idea: Samba 2406.07522, Kimi Linear 2510.26692, Qwen3-Next (Gated DeltaNet:gated attention 3:1 plus a 512-expert ultra-sparse MoE). Caveat: some full/sliding attention layers are required for precise recall; pure linear models lose it. Dormouse note: the 3:1 ratio matches the LoopBlock router blend; keep at least one spatial-attention-heavy iteration per 4.

nodes.label: Input-side table scaling is log-linear; the output side is a trap
nodes.norm_label: input-side table scaling is log-linear; the output side is a trap
nodes.rationale: Over-Tokenized Transformer finds a log-linear relation between input vocabulary (hierarchical n-gram tables) and loss, and a large input table alone recovers a 2x-size baseline, while scaling the output vocabulary hurts smaller models (arXiv:2501.16975). TN-gram replaces per-order hash tables with a tensorized CP decomposition to reduce collision interference (arXiv:2606.08347).

nodes.label: JEPA-style latent objectives at LM scale: first positive results
nodes.norm_label: jepa-style latent objectives at lm scale: first positive results
nodes.rationale: LLM-JEPA adds an EMA-free embedding-prediction loss: +14.2pp on NL-RX-SYNTH for Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 5-25pp across Gemma-2/OpenELM/OLMo, and reports overfitting robustness; pretraining experiments exist but are small-scale (arXiv:2509.14252). Dormouse: directionally supported but the gains are documented in fine-tuning, so JEPA at 0.05 is cheap insurance against collapse.

nodes.label: KDA: channel-wise decay, Diagonal-Plus-Low-Rank chunkwise, NoPE
nodes.norm_label: kda: channel-wise decay, diagonal-plus-low-rank chunkwise, nope
nodes.rationale: Kimi Delta Attention extends Gated DeltaNet with per-dimension decay and gets positional information from KDA itself, so its layers run NoPE without losing long-context quality (arXiv:2510.26692). Gated DeltaNet-2 decouples erase vs write gates and reduces to KDA when gates collapse (arXiv:2605.22791).

nodes.label: KoLeo at LM scale: no public evidence
nodes.norm_label: koleo at lm scale: no public evidence
nodes.rationale: KoLeo comes from DINOv2 vision training (arXiv:2304.07193); no 2024-2026 LM paper shows it pulling weight on top of CE. Delete or drop to a permanent-off flag; JEPA alone carries the anti-collapse story.

nodes.label: Multi-token prediction: real but size-dependent; byte-level version looks strong
nodes.norm_label: multi-token prediction: real but size-dependent; byte-level version looks strong
nodes.rationale: 13B models solve +12% HumanEval / +17% MBPP, gains grow with size so below 1B expect small effects; notably 8-byte prediction solved 67% more MBPP pass@1 than next-byte (arXiv:2404.19737). DeepSeek-V3 ships one-depth MTP (arXiv:2412.19437); Qwen3-Next trains with MTP and reports a pretraining-quality and inference-speed payoff. DSpark at K=4 is in family with this evidence.

nodes.label: Muon is the documented compute winner
nodes.norm_label: muon is the documented compute winner
nodes.rationale: Muon reaches AdamW-equal loss with ~52% of training FLOPs (fitted 2.506*C^-0.052 vs 2.608*C^-0.054); two ingredients made it scale: weight decay on matrix params and matching Muon's update RMS to AdamW's so AdamW-tuned LR/WD transfer directly (arXiv:2502.16982). Routing rule: Muon on 2D linear maps, AdamW on embeddings/heads/norms/scalars. AdEMAMix is the Adam-side upgrade for the non-Muon groups (arXiv:2409.03137) - one extra accumulator per row, which is exactly the host-RAM CPU-Adam cost. Dormouse's fp8 factor-forward interacts with the documented overfit-NaN episodes, so --quant fp32 remains the safe arm.

nodes.label: PonderNet-style halting: evidence is weak, the loop is not
nodes.norm_label: pondernet-style halting: evidence is weak, the loop is not
nodes.rationale: The original PonderNet validated on algorithmic/bAbI-scale tasks only (arXiv:2107.05407); a 2026 audit found the apparent advantage of learned halting annihilates to +0.000 across 31 configurations once the readout is equalized, so the value lies in the recurrent refinement, not the halting head (arXiv:2608.22347). MoR replaced halting with per-token depth routers and won.

nodes.label: Precision: the low-bit window is real but has a floor
nodes.norm_label: precision: the low-bit window is real but has a floor
nodes.rationale: 465 runs, 3-16 bit: lower training precision lowers effective parameter count with saturating returns around 6-8 bits; both 16-bit and sub-4-bit training are suboptimal; low-precision degradation grows with overtraining, which is dormouse's known failure mode (arXiv:2411.04330). bf16 storage + fp32 accumulation + fp32 heads stays the default.

nodes.label: Top 10 highest-leverage moves for dormouse
nodes.rationale: 1 quality-filter the corpus then dedup (largest single lever, strong); 2 adopt a DataDecide/RegMix protocol (low cost, the multiplier); 3 space/entropy-patched trunk; 4 keep and grow input-side Engram tables, never output-side; 5 distill from a downloaded open teacher; 6 Muon+ with update-RMS matching; 7 fine-grain the MoE; 8 up to 4 epochs; 9 replace the halt head with routers or keep fixed depth; 10 A/B an energy head. Process note: rows 1, 2 and 8 cost no architecture work and compound; at this scale data and measurement discipline out-earn new mechanisms.

nodes.label: TSCT low-rank expert bodies: no direct public pretraining win
nodes.norm_label: tsct low-rank expert bodies: no direct public pretraining win
nodes.rationale: Fine-grained MoE gains are documented with plain small FFN experts; TSCT-style spectral low-rank expert factors have no 2024-2026 public comparison at matched active params. Treat TSCT as an unproven swap and A/B against plain fine-grained SwiGLU experts at matched params.

nodes.label: Weight-shared recurrent depth has real evidence at small scale
nodes.norm_label: weight-shared recurrent depth has real evidence at small scale
nodes.rationale: Mixture-of-Recursions sets a Pareto frontier at 135M-1.7B with middle-cycle parameter sharing as the best layout (arXiv:2507.10524); a 3.5B recurrent-depth model improves sharply with test-time iterations (ARC 49% at r=4 to ~70% at r=32, arXiv:2502.05171); EBT reports ~35% faster scaling and +29% more gain from inference compute (arXiv:2507.02092).

nodes.label: Muon ns 8->5 and retract_every 1->4: hygiene, not a lever
nodes.norm_label: muon ns 8->5 and retract_every 1->4: hygiene, not a lever
nodes.rationale: Standard Muon runs 5 Newton-Schulz iterations; dormouse pins MUON_NS_STEPS = 8. opt 111 ms + retract 105 ms = 216 ms = ~3% of the step, already at the low end of the published 2-17% band. Polar Express reaches the same accuracy at identical wall clock (arXiv:2505.16932), Gram-NS cuts orthogonalization 40-50% (arXiv via tridao.me), NS runs routinely in bf16. Masters stay fp32 and only the forward path is quantized - that matches every cited recipe.

nodes.label: burn-gdn2 Gated DeltaNet 2
nodes.rationale: Claims a 'Linear-complexity recurrent token mixer' (O(T) instead of O(T^2)) implementing Gated DeltaNet 2. Channel-wise erase gate b_t (key axis) and write gate w_t (value axis) replace the scalar write-strength gate; alpha_t is the per-channel decay from A_log and softplus(F(x)+dt_bias). Claims two custom cubecl kernels (gdn2_chunk_intra_kernel, gdn2_chunk_inter_kernel) replace the per-chunk tensor-op loop on the bare CUDA backend (CudaBare), with other backends falling back to the tensor path. Claims an exact fused autodiff op (one graph node, matrix-level WY adjoint, M^-1 reuse) worth ~3-5x end-to-end on CUDA and ~5-10x over the tensor path alone (~16k tracked nodes removed). Claims 1000-case bit-exact reference tests and bit-exact token-by-token decode equivalence. Extra beyond the paper: min_decay per-channel decay floor, GVA, allow_neg_eigval. Benchmarks (RTX 5060 Ti, fp32) claim: tensor path 2.3-3.7x vs pure PyTorch chunked ops; fused kernels ~2-18x vs NVlabs Triton chunk_gdn2; full module forward ~58-800x vs PyTorch full chunked; fused-op training 9.1-51x vs PyTorch; ~1.2k tok/s single-token decode; roughly half the activation memory at d=2048/T=4096 (~330 MB vs ~565 MB). K3-style exp(cumsum(g)) underflow limits the fused kernel to chunk <= 16.

nodes.label: burn-kda Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) for Burn
nodes.norm_label: burn-kda kimi delta attention (kda) for burn
nodes.rationale: Claims a 'Complete implementation of Kimi Delta Attention (KDA)' (Kimi Linear and Kimi K3 section 2.1.1, Eqs 1-6). KDA extends the gated delta rule with a channel-wise forget gate and a data-dependent write strength beta_t^h = Sigmoid(W_beta^h x_t), per-head and per-token, 'not a global scalar'. Two channel-wise decay mappings from a low-rank logit z_t = W_alpha^down(W_alpha^up x_t) + b_alpha with rank = head_dim: DecayFn::Softplus (Kimi Linear, g = -exp(A_h) Softplus(z), alpha in (0,1)) and DecayFn::Sigmoid (K3, g = g_min Sigmoid(exp(A_h) z), fixed g_min = -5, alpha in (e^-5,1), claimed 'bounded, numerically safe'). q/k = L2Norm(Swish(ShortConv(Wx))), v = Swish(ShortConv(W_v x)); output gate y = W_o [Sigmoid(W_g x) * RMSNorm(o_t)] with GateMode::FullRank (K3) or GateMode::LowRank (Kimi Linear Eq 10). Training and decoding both use the chunked WY form, claimed 'identical algebra to GDN-2 under the mapping b = beta, g = log(alpha), w = beta'. Claims a fused CUDA path that reuses the GDN-2 chunked kernels through the same WY mapping (no value-gate trick: U carries beta as the value gate) and that forward_train_fused runs the whole chunked WY recurrence as ONE autodiff node through burn-gdn2 0.7's fused op with an exact matrix-level backward that never re-runs the forward. Numerical stability contract: with g_min = -5 a naive chunk of 64 accumulates log-decay to -320 and 1/Gamma = exp(320) overflows f32, so the tensor chunk path computes decay tile-locally in log space with inter-tile weights exp(G_p - G_q) <= 1 and solves the WY system per 16-token tile, making any chunk size exact (chunk 64 = the K3 paper setting is supported), while the fused CUDA kernel is only stable up to chunk_size = 16 and falls back to the tensor path above that. Benchmarks (RTX 5060 Ti, attention core only) claim forward 15-40x faster than the fla chunk_kda Triton reference (0.05-0.10 ms vs 1.0-2.1 ms) and module train 0.36-0.43 ms = 7-24x faster than the Triton reference's raw attention-core train. States FlashKDA's CUTLASS path was not buildable here (needs a CUDA 12.8 toolkit matching torch cu128). Claims 10 unit tests and 3 CUDA tests (fused == tensor chunk, fused == decode for both mappings).

nodes.label: burn-mhc Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
nodes.rationale: Claims a full implementation of mHC: Eq 3 n-stream residual x_{l+1} = H_res x_l + (H_post)^T F(H_pre x_l); Eq 7 first-order hyper-network mapping RMSNorm(vec(x)) through linear projections + static biases with gating factors alpha init 0.01; Eq 8 H_pre = sigmoid, H_post = 2*sigmoid (non-negativity prevents signal cancellation); Eq 9 Sinkhorn-Knopp entropic projection (SINKHORN_ITERS = t_max = 20) onto the Birkhoff polytope so H_res is doubly stochastic (row/col sums 1, spectral norm <= 1, compositional closure), 'restoring the identity-mapping property'. At init the block reduces to the standard residual h + sum of branches. Exports MhcBlock, sinkhorn_knopp, SINKHORN_ITERS, ALPHA_INIT. Performance claims (RTX 3090, CUDA): the 20-iteration Sinkhorn is fused into one launch per (batch, time) matrix, forward 32.4 ms -> 1.65 us (19,600x) and 104.7 ms -> 2.55 us (41,000x); backward 67.1 ms -> 17.7 ms (4x) with the 2*iters normalizations reversed from per-step sums kept in shared memory. Verification claims: fused == tensor path and doubly stochastic (<1e-2), fused backward == tensor backward (<1e-3). Single tracked node under Autodiff<Cuda>; forward-only builds use the bare CUDA fused kernel.

nodes.label: burn-mod Mixture-of-Depths for Burn
nodes.rationale: Claims to implement Mixture-of-Depths: a per-block router emits a scalar weight per token, the k highest-weighted tokens (expert-choice routing) run through the block (self-attention + MLP) and the rest pass through a residual connection; the block output is scaled by the router weight, putting the router on the gradient path (paper eq. 1). Exports ModRouter (linear d -> 1 token router), select_topk (expert-choice top-k selection, masked-argmax, GPU-safe), route_block (eq. 1 routing step around any block closure), bce_aux_loss (binary cross-entropy aux loss for causal autoregressive sampling, paper section 3.5), ModPredictor (optional stop-gradient MLP predictor for sampling, paper section 3.5). No speed, memory or fused-kernel claims.

nodes.label: burn-mor Mixture-of-Recursions
nodes.rationale: Claims per-token adaptive recursion depth on a single shared stack of layers. Explicitly scoped: 'This crate provides the pure-tensor routing pieces; the recursion block itself is your own (parameter-shared) layer stack.' Exports MoRConfig (keep_frac 0.5, block_size 128, aux_weight 0.01, gradient_detach true), MoRRouter (Linear d -> 1, no bias, importance scorer), select_active (top-k active/inactive split, no gather_nd, CUDA-safe), gather_active ([B,T,D]+[B,K] -> dense [B,K,D]), scatter_active, load_balancing_loss (mean squared deviation of per-token active usage from n/T, differentiable through the router scores). select_active keeps round(keep_frac * T) of the still-active tokens (hierarchical filtering), so deeper levels operate on progressively smaller active sets. Per the paper's KV-sharing variant (default ON), KV pairs are cached once for all tokens at the first recursion and reused at deeper levels; only the query set shrinks. Contract: all functions are pure tensor ops, no host branching, no into_data, generic over Backend, compose with Autodiff. No speed or kernel claims; tests are assert-based self-checks on the ndarray backend.

nodes.label: burn-parcae spectral retention for stable looped models
nodes.norm_label: burn-parcae spectral retention for stable looped models
nodes.rationale: Claims to implement the Parcae stability mechanism for looped (parameter-shared, iterative) transformers: recast looping as a nonlinear time-variant dynamical system h_{t+1} = A_bar*h_t + B_bar*e + R_bar(h_t, e), then constrain A_bar by discretizing a continuous-time negative-diagonal parameterization: A := diag(-exp(a)) with a learnable per-channel log-rate, A_bar := exp(delta*A) with a learnable per-channel step size delta > 0, B_bar := delta*B with B unconstrained (the input is LayerNorm'd). Claims this gives 'guaranteed contraction, bounded residual dynamics for ANY loop count T, by construction' -- all eigenvalues of exp(delta*A) lie in (0,1), with 'no clipping, no post-hoc normalization'. Exports SpectralRetentionConfig (full_b: the paper's full dxd injection matrix vs the parameter-efficient diagonal variant, default diagonal), SpectralRetention (retention(), inject(e), forward(h,e)), and the free fn retention_matrix(a, delta). Contract: pure tensor ops, zero host branching in forward (exp, neg, mul, add only); defaults a = 0, delta = 1 give A_bar ~ 0.37, a mild contraction; gradients flow through exp freely, nothing clipped. No speed or fused-kernel claims.

nodes.label: burn-ptrn Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
nodes.rationale: Claims test-time scaling for recursive (looped, parameter-shared) models with 'no retraining of loop weights', in three steps: (1) recurrent Gaussian noise eps ~ N(0, sigma^2 I) injected into the latent at every recursion step (sigma ~ 0.2-1.0 by task), noise-only with no gradient term, claimed to let ~8% of rollouts escape bad basins; (2) best-Q@K selection over K parallel rollouts, each scored by a learned Q-head, taking the argmax trajectory, with the claim that 'width scaling is stronger and more practical than depth scaling'; (3) joint Q-head training L_step = CE(f_O(y), y_true) + BCE(q_hat, 1[y_hat = y_true]) so Q separates correct from incorrect rollouts. Exports PtrnConfig (noise_sigma 0.5, num_rollouts 16, tau 1.0), QHead (Linear(d,1): logit, prob, q_loss masked BCE), add_recurrent_noise, best_of_k (q_logits [K,B,T,1] + rollouts [K,B,T,D] -> ([B,T,D],[B] Int)), correctness_target. Contract: all primitives are pure tensor ops with no host branching, dropping into any burn training or recursive inference loop. No fused-kernel or speed claims; labeled a research crate for the aria project.

nodes.label: burn-rmsnorm RMS Normalization for Burn
nodes.rationale: Claims 'Root mean square layer normalization' as a simpler, faster alternative to LayerNorm used in every major LLM (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma) -- no measured numbers. Formula: RMS(x) = sqrt(mean(x^2) + eps), y = x / RMS(x) * weight; explicitly does not re-center (no mean subtraction), only re-scales. Exports RMSNorm::new(512, 1e-5, &device) with forward mapping [B, T, 512] -> [B, T, 512]. No fused-kernel claims.

So adaptive depth is not 'easy tokens skip' (that is pure compute) — it is 'a few hard items get more depth than the fixed budget gives them'. nodes.norm_label: the diminishing returns of early-exit decoding in modern llms arxiv 2603.23701
nodes.rationale: The honest prior for early exit. Effectiveness DECREASES across newer model generations, is HIGHER for larger models (notably >20B), higher for dense than MoE/SSM, and higher for base pretrained than tuned models. A 7.5M base model is the favourable end on architecture/recipe and the unfavourable end on scale.

nodes.norm_label: dual-trajectory objective (full deep path + sampled shortcut, stop-gradient logit consistency)
nodes.rationale: LoopFormer's L_cons is a stop-gradient per-token-logit consistency loss pulling the short trajectory onto the long one. The only published recipe that ties short trajectories to the deep one. Collapse-resistant: the target's own CE is in the loss at full weight, so making the target garbage cannot game it. Failure mode is waste (depth 4 degenerating to depth 1), visible in the depth curve.

Fix: allocate with dev_ad = normed_l.device(). Inner-adjoint seed is now dy (= dh_flat*rs) and d_raw is packed to the [bt,2] gate columns.

nodes.label: argtopk emits the u32::MAX null-accumulator sentinel as an index
nodes.norm_label: argtopk emits the u32::max null-accumulator sentinel as an index
nodes.rationale: Tensor::argtopk on a cubecl backend emits out-of-range indices for any row with fewer than k values above -inf, and the gather then faults (cuEventCreate 700 / CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS). Not a cast bug, not an off-by-one: a sentinel. to_output_parallel/perpendicular casts the coordinate straight to the index dtype where u32::MAX becomes -1 (i32) or 4294967295 (i64/u32).

nodes.label: Vendored cubek-reduce patch: reaches, output clamp, null seed
nodes.norm_label: vendored cubek-reduce patch: reaches, output clamp, null seed
nodes.rationale: Patched in the kernel rather than at any call site, through the existing [patch.crates-io] pattern. (1) reaches: a slot still holding min_value is empty, not full. (2) to_output_parallel + to_output_perpendicular: clamp the coordinate to axis_len - 1 on the way out - the load-bearing invariant guard, placed in the unused shape_axis_reduce parameter. (3) null_accumulator: seed the coordinate at 0. Cost: one extra comparison per emitted index.

nodes.label: The reaches fast-path guard is the pre.3 -> pre.4 regression
nodes.norm_label: the reaches fast-path guard is the pre.3 -> pre.4 regression
nodes.rationale: cubek-reduce 0.3.0-pre.4 wraps every topk_insert in if !(item < kth) { any = true } with kth = elements[k-1]. Sound for a full list, wrong for an empty slot, because -inf < min_value is a TRUE comparison: a masked candidate is judged unable to enter a slot waiting for its first element, so the slot keeps u32::MAX. pre.3 had no guard and always displaced the min_value seed. The guard was added as a measured win (151936-wide logits row, 4.7 ms on GP100) and its doc comment reasons about NaN without noticing -inf reaches the same state. Two smaller holes share the root: k > axis length, and plane_topk_merge building its u32::MAX phantom by construction.

nodes.norm_label: topk_gather / topk_indices_last with the in-range guarantee

Tests run on ndarray AND cuda from one body with adversarial rows (all-equal, single hot index, k == n, k = 1, all -inf, -inf prefix with 3 visible candidates at k = 8). The CUDA arm is the point: ndarray's argtopk was always correct, which is why the failure stayed invisible. k > n is now safe but not meaningful; ties are unordered by contract.

nodes.label: Hard rule 3: beat the original on speed and on VRAM
nodes.norm_label: hard rule 3: beat the original on speed and on vram
nodes.rationale: Bit-for-bit identical output is the FLOOR. Each crate carries a benchmark against its reference on the shapes we actually run (batch 10 x seq 512, 12 heads, K=V=64, chunk 16, fp32 and bf16), reporting step time and peak VRAM. First measured case: our gated-delta path allocates 17 fresh tensors / 248 MB scratch per call, ~1 GB per step, against a high-water pool that never frees, which is why KDA is ~80% of a step while the fused kernels have an 80-100 us design floor; the reference (FLA) avoids materialising a 63 MB per-chunk state export by recomputing it. A 200x effect that no kernel tuning reaches. Also forbids writing a kernel before roofline arithmetic (memory bound at 3.1 FLOP/byte vs machine balance 24) and re-implementing a mechanism that already exists in the fork.

nodes.label: Hard rule 1: strictly per the research paper, bit-for-bit vs the original source
nodes.norm_label: hard rule 1: strictly per the research paper, bit-for-bit vs the original source
nodes.rationale: FLA for the gated-delta / linear-attention family, the authors' repos for everything else, to a stated and justified tolerance. Where no reference code exists, the crate says so in its doc comment instead of implying verification it does not have. A rule about honesty as much as numerics - the inventory found a crate whose headline numbers are verbatim-correct from a paper's table but omit the number that governs our A/B.

nodes.label: Hard rule 2: zero host-device synchronization
nodes.rationale: No CPU in the hot path: no try_into_scalar, into_data, blocking_read, try_for_each, or host-side branch on a device value. Every host-visible quantity comes from a device counter or flag read at a declared cadence. Not a micro-optimization: a per-step scalar read added to the NaN firewall on 2026-09-27 was removed the same day because it serializes CPU against GPU on a launch-bound workload. Where a decision depends on a device value the decision is made ON the device (burn-muon-plus zero-gradient rule uses mask_fill).

nodes.label: Collapse-proof-by-construction test: does a learned quantity scale the loss, and is the target recomputed each step?
nodes.norm_label: collapse-proof-by-construction test: does a learned quantity scale the loss, and is the target recomputed each step?
nodes.rationale: Applied to every rung: 'there is no learned quantity that scales the loss… nothing to shrink'. A MoR-lite trained end-to-end with no aux BCE reintroduces the scale channel the aux loss closes — capacity still fills the top-k, so it degrades to ARBITRARY selection rather than collapse: milder, but still a silent bug (MoR's failure catalogue: dead tokens, MaxVio, NaN rows).

nodes.label: Cumulative-softmax depth threshold router (2-layer MLP on initial hidden state; token active iff p^(i) = Σ_{l≥i} π_l > 0.5)
nodes.norm_label: cumulative-softmax depth threshold router (2-layer mlp on initial hidden state; token active iff p^(i) = σ_{l≥i} π_l > 0.5)
nodes.rationale: T-LoopFormer's router shape, judged the cleanest 2026 collapse-proof example: no depth loss term at all (no penalty, no prior, no loss-mass mixture), nested selection A1 ⊇ A2 ⊇ …, so there is no scalar to shrink. Depth-1 requires π1 > 0.5 and got only 0.23% of tokens. Decision uses only the token itself → causal.

nodes.label: Expert-choice top-k with fixed β-percentile capacity: exactly k tokens always get through
nodes.norm_label: expert-choice top-k with fixed β-percentile capacity: exactly k tokens always get through
nodes.rationale: Rank-based and capacity-fixed, so no global mass the optimizer can shrink. No depth-0 mode (every token traverses recursion 1), and the LM loss is computed once at each token's final depth. Anti-collapse properties are structural, not incidental.

nodes.label: Penalty-based halting collapses to the floor: ACT and PonderNet both hit 49.96 @ 1.00 loop — exactly dormouse's failure, on a different backbone
nodes.norm_label: penalty-based halting collapses to the floor: act and pondernet both hit 49.96 @ 1.00 loop — exactly dormouse's failure, on a different backbone
nodes.rationale: Adding a floor makes ACT/PonderNet EXACTLY fixed depth (54.71 @ 2.00, Δ = 0): the machinery then buys nothing. The floor was selected so it coincides with the best fixed depth.

nodes.label: Rung 4 — oracle-distilled decider p_t = σ(w^T z_t + b), d ≈ 512 params, BCE on the RecurTrace target, hard floor T_min = 2
nodes.norm_label: rung 4 — oracle-distilled decider p_t = σ(w^t z_t + b), d ≈ 512 params, bce on the recurtrace target, hard floor t_min = 2
nodes.rationale: Three independent collapse-resistance reasons: (i) the target is a MEASURED per-batch quantity recomputed every step, the same anchoring that keeps MoR's router scores bimodal; (ii) the LM loss is not weighted by p_t — no loss-mass knob; (iii) the floor makes depth-1 unreachable by construction. Kill criteria: mean depth pinned at the floor for >90% of inputs after warmup; the fake-loss canary fires; T_min set to the best fixed depth merely reaches fixed-depth parity.

nodes.label: dormouse PonderNet halting collapse (the two measured failures behind ADR-0013)
nodes.norm_label: dormouse pondernet halting collapse (the two measured failures behind adr-0013)
nodes.rationale: Root of the whole design problem: the p-weighted loss mixture is a knob that multiplies the loss and can be shrunk to zero; eval was frozen at uniform depth.

nodes.label: p-weighted loss mixture (PonderNet Σ p_n·CE_n) — the collapse channel
nodes.norm_label: p-weighted loss mixture (pondernet σ p_n·ce_n) — the collapse channel
nodes.rationale: A learned quantity that scales the loss can be shrunk by the optimizer — the exact difference between a mechanism that collapsed for us and MoR/RecurTrace, which compute the LM loss once, unweighted, at the token's final depth.

nodes.norm_label: auxiliary bce on the main router with the router's own top-k membership as target (keeps scores bimodal at {0,1})

nodes.norm_label: adr-0013 fixed depth (pondernet halting deleted after two measured collapses)

nodes.label: CORRECTION: ADR-0013's MoR 135M reason was wrong; the rejection stands on a different ground (the sm_120 per-depth gather)
nodes.norm_label: correction: adr-0013's mor 135m reason was wrong; the rejection stands on a different ground (the sm_120 per-depth gather)
nodes.rationale: The isoFLOP table (135M base, N_r=3, 2e18 FLOPs, FineWeb NLL) separates the two causes: Vanilla 106M/30 layers 3.0922, Recursive 42M/1+10+1 3.2058, MoR 42M/1+10+1 3.1077. At 5e18: 2.9464 / 3.0534 / 3.0192. So MoR BEATS the same-architecture recursive baseline at every scale including 135M; the deficit is against a 2.5×-larger unshared transformer and is a recursion (weight-sharing) effect, not a router effect. Does not change the verdict, changes the reason — and the reason was written into an ADR.

nodes.norm_label: distillation beats supervised pretraining when a teacher exists
nodes.rationale: With an existing teacher, distillation dominates supervised training up to a predictable compute level; if the teacher must also be trained, supervised wins; a too-strong teacher eventually hurts (capacity gap, arXiv:2502.08606). The optimal teacher sits near 2.5x the student (arXiv:2311.07052). Method: on-policy GKD with reverse KL/JSD on student rollouts (arXiv:2306.13649).

nodes.label: Off-accelerator lookup tables are a published, winning recipe
nodes.norm_label: off-accelerator lookup tables are a published, winning recipe
nodes.rationale: SCONE stores frequent-n-gram embeddings off-accelerator with O(1) lookups; a 1B accelerator-resident model beats a 1.9B dense baseline at ~half the FLOPs and memory and loss drops monotonically with table scale (arXiv:2502.01637). DeepSeek's Engram frames the same module as a third sparsity axis (arXiv:2601.07372). Memory Layers at Scale beats dense with 2x compute and beats MoE at matched compute/params, largest gains on factual QA (arXiv:2412.09764). This is the exact pattern dormouse's host-RAM Engram implements, including Adam-without-weight-decay on tables - kept because it costs nothing, not because it is independently replicated.

nodes.label: Hashed tables: host RAM is forced at 48M rows
nodes.norm_label: hashed tables: host ram is forced at 48m rows
nodes.rationale: At 48M rows (1.54B params, 18.4 GB with fp32 params + Adam m/v) the tables cannot fit a 16 GB card, so the Meta-style on-GPU product-key table is not on the table; Engram's deterministic addressing is exactly what makes host offloading viable. The measured +2.3% step cost for every-step host-Adam is consistent, so the transfer is not the bottleneck; the unfused GPU-side gather and row-grad scatter-add are.

nodes.label: Decaying survival probability p_l = 1 − (l/L)(1 − p_L), p_L = 0.5, + test-time re-weighting

nodes.rationale: Huang Eq. 4/5: earlier layers get higher survival ('should therefore be more reliably present'); uniformly vs decaying compared empirically, decaying kept. Test time re-weights each unit by p_l. nodes.label: Missing-state problem: copying K/V from lower layers into skipped layers collapses to 23.02 ROUGE-L

In dormouse an early-exited predecessor has no K/V at loops 2..4, and the KDA state is a delta-rule state, so copy-forward is a design decision, not a freebie. Sequence-level (per-row) exit has none of this.

nodes.norm_label: nobody has published a byte-level post-training result at any scale
nodes.rationale: arXiv API queries return only ByT5-style task fine-tuning and hobby national-model reports; confirmed absent, not merely un-found. The nearest byte-level data point is ufakzeka-1's byte-level TOKENIZER at 151M, with SFT-only post-training. Consequence: dormouse's entire ladder is extrapolation.
