nodes.norm_label: scale gap: 7.5m is 16x below the smallest end-to-end sft+rl pipeline
nodes.rationale: smallest published end-to-end SFT+RL = nanochat d12 at ~124M (dormouse is 16x below); dormouse is ~60x below the smallest published RLVR success. Nobody has published a post-training ablation at 100M-7.5M. Honest expectation: Stage 1 is a learning exercise, not a capability jump, and the growth plan to 100M-1B is the actual recipe. Mitigated only by >=3 seeds per arm.

nodes.label: Byte models need a wire protocol: role delimiters on control bytes
nodes.norm_label: byte models need a wire protocol: role delimiters on control bytes
nodes.rationale: nanochat's <|assistant_start|>/<|assistant_end|> and SmolLM3's ChatML are BPE SPECIAL TOKENS - free, unambiguous, impossible to confuse with user text. A byte model has no such escape. Pick role delimiters that cannot occur in the corpus (control bytes 0x00-0x08 are near-certainly absent from UTF-8 text) and make the loss mask a function of those bytes. SmolLM3's finding that XML-tool and Python-tool schemas want separate template sections is a free win here: with no tokenizer to disambiguate them, section boundaries must be explicit byte markers.

nodes.label: ChatCORE: a cheap capability gate, not response length
nodes.norm_label: chatcore: a cheap capability gate, not response length
nodes.rationale: nanochat's ChatCORE = mean centered accuracy over ARC-Easy / ARC-Challenge / MMLU / GSM8K / HumanEval, normalized against the 0.25 / 0.0 random baselines, reported as an aggregate plus a categorical-only variant. The report pairs it with SimpleRL-Zoo's finding that length is not capability: track a capability metric, not response length.

nodes.label: Decontamination and dev/unseen eval splits as a copyable practice
nodes.norm_label: decontamination and dev/unseen eval splits as a copyable practice
nodes.rationale: Tulu 3's multi-task eval scheme with development and unseen splits plus substantial decontamination. Rufus-Air's chain: 8-gram chain of passes + exhaustive 8-gram + dense Llama-NV-Embed retrieval on math/knowledge, removing 4,187 unique samples. For dormouse the operational form is: hold out eval bytes BEFORE building any post-training data, and run a decontamination script before every build.

nodes.label: dormouse: 7.5M byte-level LM (vocab 256) targeting 100M-1B universal assistant
nodes.norm_label: dormouse: 7.5m byte-level lm (vocab 256) targeting 100m-1b universal assistant
nodes.rationale: The system the whole report is an input to: byte-level next-byte LM, 7.5M params today, goal 100M-1B, must become a universal assistant (coding, math, physics, agentic computer use, browsing). Constraints that shape every recommendation: byte-level output (no tokenizer), a very short context budget for tool trajectories, and an in-model n-gram memory table (the Engram) that already drives train CE to ~0 while held-out stays hard.

nodes.label: Rufus-Air's four load-bearing principles worth copying
nodes.norm_label: rufus-air's four load-bearing principles worth copying
nodes.rationale: SFT-as-capability-floor, learnability filtering, reward-reliability ordering, infra-is-the-recipe. All four are correct and all four are cheap to adopt; the 8-stage serial shape, the 27B-token SFT mix and the sandbox fleet are 4-5 orders of magnitude out of reach.

nodes.label: Honest uncertainty, ranked 1-7 for dormouse
nodes.rationale: Ranked list: (1) zero byte-level post-training results exist at any scale, so the whole ladder is extrapolation and the first risk is format; (2) 7.5M is 16x below the smallest end-to-end SFT+RL pipeline and 60x below the smallest RLVR success - Stage 1 is a learning exercise, >=3 seeds per arm; (3) capacity ceilings are real, not a data gap; (4) serial vs mixed is unresolved but moot at dormouse's compute; (5) the SFT-floor doctrine is contested at small scale - keep Stage 0, budget the A/B; (6) browsing / open-web search RL is untested below 100B and costs hundreds of dollars per pass; (7) the Engram near-optimum risk is dormouse-specific and unpublished.

nodes.label: Invariant: infra is part of the recipe
nodes.norm_label: invariant: infra is part of the recipe
nodes.rationale: Rufus-Air: token-in/token-out on-policy multi-turn rollouts, stateful sandboxes, Rollout Routing Replay for the MoE. INTELLECT-3: async-only prime-rl plus sub-10s sandboxes with provisioning overlapped with first-turn reasoning. MiMo-V2.6: environment hardening, adversarial screening, verifier cross-checks. None of this is an add-on; for dormouse the cheap instance is nanochat's in-process execution.py, which needs none of INTELLECT-3's container fleet.

nodes.label: Loss mask = assistant bytes only (never prompts or tool observations)
nodes.norm_label: loss mask = assistant bytes only (never prompts or tool observations)
nodes.rationale: nanochat SFT: mask=0 for user prompts, BOS, special tokens AND tool outputs. nanochat RL: 'Prompt tokens and forced tool-use tokens get mask=0, so they carry no loss' - identical to the SFT rule. SmolLM3 likewise masks user turns and tool results. For a byte model this is a function of chosen role delimiter bytes, which is why the delimiters have to be designed first.

nodes.label: The 2026 convergent tail: mixed RL, then multi-teacher OPD
nodes.norm_label: the 2026 convergent tail: mixed rl, then multi-teacher opd
nodes.rationale: What has converged across four independent orgs: one mixed RL run, then multi-teacher on-policy distillation for whatever the verifiers cannot see. Rufus-Air itself names multi-teacher OPD as the unexplored alternative in §6; Nemotron shipped it as MOPD, MiMo as MOPD2, SEA-LION v4.8 as online OPD. This is the one place the report says dormouse should copy the 2026 frontier rather than Rufus-Air.

nodes.label: nanochat RL stage hyperparameters (chat_rl.py, ~250 lines)
nodes.rationale: GSM8K train only, 1 epoch, reward = a programmatic check on the decoded string. examples_per_step 16 total across ranks, num_samples 16 per example (group size 16), max_new_tokens 256, temperature 1.0, top-k 50. init-lr-frac 0.05 - RL RUNS AT 5% OF THE SFT/BASE LR. LR is a simple rampdown to zero, no warmup. Muon matrix_lr 0.02, Adam embedding_lr 0.2 / unembedding_lr 0.004, weight_decay 0.0. Advantages are rewards - rewards.mean() per group; PG objective is sum(logp * advantage) / num_valid_tokens. The docstring names the simplification: no trust region, no KL, on-policy so no PPO ratio+clip, DAPO-style token-level (not sequence-level) normalization, and (r - mu) instead of z-score (r - mu)/sigma. Prompt tokens and forced tool-use tokens get mask=0. README caveat: float16 auto-enables a GradScaler and 'SFT supports this too but RL currently does not' - a grad-scaler gap on the RL path is exactly the underflow hazard that matters at dormouse's LR and batch size.

nodes.label: nanochat SFT stage hyperparameters (chat_sft.py)
nodes.rationale: Mixture: SmolTalk(train) 460K rows x1 general conversation, MMLU(auxiliary_train) 100K x3 multiple-choice format, GSM8K(main,train) 8K x4 'teaches Math and Tool Use' - a ~460K chat : 32K math-with-tool-use ratio (~14:1). Hyperparameters, all explicit defaults: max_seq_len 2048, total_batch_size 524288 tokens, init-lr-frac 0.8, warmup_ratio 0.0, warmdown_ratio 0.5, final_lr_frac 0.0, weight_decay 0.0, Muon momentum ramped 0.85->0.95 over 300 iters, Adam for embedding/unembedding (0.3 / 0.004), Muon for matrices (0.02). Optimizer momentum buffers are warm-started from pretraining but LRs are restored afterwards, because pretraining's warmdown leaves LRs near zero. Packing is BOS-aligned best-fit and rows are padded, never cropped, so no token is silently discarded. 2-4 epochs recommended for dormouse's Stage 0.

nodes.label: Invariant: one output format end-to-end, loss mask fixed at SFT
nodes.norm_label: invariant: one output format end-to-end, loss mask fixed at sft
nodes.rationale: Rufus-Air keeps the chat template consistent from SFT through the agent stages, with a role-aware schema and per-message loss mask. nanochat: the chat template, the loss mask and the tool protocol are all established in SFT and never touched by RL; the RL stage only changes the policy's arithmetic accuracy. Multi-harness mixing (MiMo-V2.6) makes this harder, not optional.

nodes.label: Process-level reward beats outcome-only by ~10pp at 0.5B
nodes.norm_label: process-level reward beats outcome-only by ~10pp at 0.5b
nodes.rationale: Qwen2.5-0.5B, GRPO, GSM8K: 63.73% process-only vs 53.75% outcome-only. Process models produce structurally consistent, arithmetically grounded traces; outcome models produce concise but derivation-error-prone chains. Caveat recorded: hybrid weights track the process weight EXCEPT lambda=0.1, which underperforms pure outcome. Bittensor's 53.3% pass@8 -> 34.8% pass@1 gap is the same headroom seen from a different angle.

nodes.label: Invariant: difficulty filtering to a productive band (0, 0.8]
nodes.norm_label: invariant: difficulty filtering to a productive band (0, 0.8]
nodes.rationale: The band every recipe independently converged on. Rufus-Air: drop prompts solved >80% before training; during training over-sample 4x and keep only groups with mean reward in (0, 0.8] (DAPO); Coding RL keeps never-solved prompts while other stages drop them. INTELLECT-3 drops pass-rate-1 groups. MiMo-V2.6 uses per-problem difficulty plus within-group ranking. SimpleRL-Zoo names query-difficulty control as one of its two key design strategies. Dormouse Stage 1 pre-filter is pass rate in (0, ~0.8].

nodes.label: Invariant: publish what did not work
nodes.norm_label: invariant: publish what did not work
nodes.rationale: Every one of the six recipes does some version of this: Rufus-Air §6 'On what the recipe does not establish', Tulu 3's 'methods that did not reliably improve performance', INTELLECT-3's no-plateau honesty plus collapse ablations, ORZ's 'extra tricks are unnecessary', and SimpleRL-Zoo, which is negative results wholesale. This is the mechanism by which the negative results in §5 exist at all.

nodes.label: dormouse recommended minimal post-training ladder (stages 0-3 + skip list)
nodes.norm_label: dormouse recommended minimal post-training ladder (stages 0-3 + skip list)
nodes.rationale: 0 Format+capability SFT (10K-100K conversations, 10-100M bytes, 2-4 epochs, ~14:1 ratio, byte-exact role delimiters, loss on assistant bytes only, ship the plateau checkpoint) -> 1 execution-grounded RLVR (1K-10K verified short coding/math prompts pre-filtered to pass rate in (0, 0.8], group 8-16, ~256 new tokens, temp 1.0, RL LR = 5% of SFT LR, no KL, no trust region, advantage = r - mu, rampdown to zero, prefer process-level reward) -> 2 on-policy distillation for anything multi-turn -> 3 DPO/APO or a 0.9/0.1 merge. SKIP until >=100M AND Stage 1 is clearly working: judge/rubric rewards, sandbox-scaled agent RL, RLHF, browsing. Sizes anchored to nanochat d12, the only published sub-200M SFT recipe.

nodes.label: Invariant: order stages by exposure to reward hacking, not by format
nodes.norm_label: invariant: order stages by exposure to reward hacking, not by format
nodes.rationale: Rufus-Air's second novelty: reward reliability sets stage ORDER. The IF stage uses an LLM-judge rubric yet runs early because the target is close to what the policy already does. Applied honestly to a 7.5M model, this ordering says the only stage worth running is the one whose reward is hardest to game and cheapest to compute: unit-test execution on short single-turn coding problems. Also the basis for dormouse's skip list.

nodes.label: Agent-sandbox fleet economics: $10K/month, 10K concurrent
nodes.rationale: Rufus-Air's cost stated honestly: a sandbox service sized for ~10K concurrent sandboxes is about $10K/month; one BrowseComp pass (1,266 questions x ~100 tool calls) is ~10^5 search+extraction calls, a few hundred dollars at list prices. This is the arithmetic behind the skip list, and behind dormouse's decision to run unit tests in-process.

nodes.label: Serial vs mixed RL: the real 2026 disagreement, unresolved
nodes.norm_label: serial vs mixed rl: the real 2026 disagreement, unresolved
nodes.rationale: Rufus-Air runs 8 serial stages; INTELLECT-3 runs one mixed RL stage; MiMo-V2.6 runs one mixed run and states the transfer rationale; Nemotron 3 Ultra runs SFT -> multi-environment RLVR -> MOPD; Domyn-Small 10B runs GRPO-VR -> DPO -> a final multi-environment GRPO across five domains. 'Nobody has shown serial > mixed or vice versa at matched compute.' Moot at dormouse's compute: with budget for one RL arm, run the single most verifiable task family, which every philosophy agrees on.

nodes.label: Invariant: the SFT floor is capability, not warm-up
nodes.norm_label: invariant: the sft floor is capability, not warm-up
nodes.rationale: Rufus-Air's strongest measured claim: SFT ckpt 3799 alone already beats the official RL-included GLM-4.5-Air release on 4 of 5 anchors. The report also holds its own epoch-1 finding: held-out scores flatten inside epoch 1 while loss keeps stepping down at each epoch boundary - ship the plateau checkpoint, not the last one. CONTESTED at small scale by two audits (see neg_sft_floor_contested).

nodes.label: Rufus-Air control: length penalty relative to the shortest correct rollout in each group
nodes.norm_label: rufus-air control: length penalty relative to the shortest correct rollout in each group
nodes.rationale: Zero at or below the shortest correct rollout in the group, linear up to a cap. Its counterpart is measured, not assumed: attaching ~10 OPTIONAL rubrics per IF instance induced a pronounced length bias, which is why Rufus-Air's rubrics describe only necessary conditions. Same anti-length-bias motive as MiMo-V2.6's GAR moving advantage toward higher-quality/shorter passing trajectories, and the same hazard SimpleRL-Zoo reports (CoT elongation to farm reward).

nodes.label: Skip list: judge/rubric, sandbox agent RL, RLHF, browsing
nodes.norm_label: skip list: judge/rubric, sandbox agent rl, rlhf, browsing
nodes.rationale: Deferred until >=100M and Stage 1 is clearly working. Two independent reasons: they are the most gameable by Rufus-Air's own ordering principle (its Search Agent is the one LLM-judge soft stage and runs second-to-last), and the most expensive in wall clock - $10K/month for ~10K concurrent sandboxes, and one BrowseComp pass (1,266 questions x ~100 tool calls) is ~10^5 search+extraction calls, a few hundred dollars at list prices. Nothing below 100B has been shown to do browsing RL.

nodes.label: Stage 1: execution-grounded RLVR on short single-turn code + math
nodes.norm_label: stage 1: execution-grounded rlvr on short single-turn code + math
nodes.rationale: Hardest-to-game reward, cheapest to compute. Binary unit tests in a local sandbox; dormouse needs none of INTELLECT-3's sub-10s container fleet - nanochat's in-process execution.py is enough. RL LR = 5% of SFT LR is the load-bearing number, taken from nanochat's init-lr-frac 0.05. Process-level reward where possible: worth ~10pp over outcome-only at 0.5B.

nodes.label: Stage 3: DPO/APO or a 0.9/0.1 merge as cheap insurance
nodes.norm_label: stage 3: dpo/apo or a 0.9/0.1 merge as cheap insurance
nodes.rationale: On-policy preference pairs, or merge 0.9/0.1 as SmolLM3 did (0.9 APO-soup / 0.1 mid-training checkpoint) to repair collateral damage APO caused - it recovered the RULER score APO had destroyed. SmolLM3 shipped this at 3B instead of RL.

nodes.label: Sub-1B verdict: evidence is real, thin, and now contested
nodes.norm_label: sub-1b verdict: evidence is real, thin, and now contested
nodes.rationale: The prior report's answer ('sub-1B evidence is thin but real, all RLVR or SFT-only') is right but understates how much has appeared. One clean negative at ~135M (L20-Edu). No published ablation at 100M-7.5M. No published byte-level result at any scale. The sub-1B successes are all RLVR or SFT-only; the multi-turn agentic results are all 4B+.

nodes.label: What separates working sub-1B RLVR from the failures: three things
nodes.norm_label: what separates working sub-1b rlvr from the failures: three things
nodes.rationale: RLVR that measurably works at 0.5-0.6B exists (SimpleRL-Zoo 0.5B, SOD 0.6B at 26% AIME25, MBPP at 0.6B/1B +13pp, nanochat d12). The difference from the failure cases is always the same three things: a pre-existing parseable format (from SFT), a dense or process-level reward, and a difficulty band.

nodes.label: Tool use is carried inside the math task, not a separate agentic dataset
nodes.norm_label: tool use is carried inside the math task, not a separate agentic dataset
nodes.rationale: nanochat's critical structural fact: GSM8K solutions execute Python via a sandboxed execution.py with tests, and 8K rows x 4 epochs is what teaches the model to emit and consume tool calls. Dormouse Stage 0 inherits the ~14:1 chat-to-math-with-tool-execution ratio. The cheapest possible way to buy a tool protocol without a separate agentic data pipeline.

nodes.label: ufakzeka-1: capacity ceilings are real, not a data gap
nodes.norm_label: ufakzeka-1: capacity ceilings are real, not a data gap
nodes.rationale: Measured at 151M: data rounds repaired only what was absent - identity tracking over long context and multi-turn arithmetic did not move under ANY data change, 'which we read as limits of the model size rather than gaps in the data.' Direct consequence for dormouse: if multi-step tool use does not emerge post-training at 7.5M, that is the expected capacity outcome, not a recipe failure. This reframes Stage 1 as a learning exercise.

nodes.label: Verdict: Rufus-Air is the best-documented recipe, not the best-transferring one
nodes.norm_label: verdict: rufus-air is the best-documented recipe, not the best-transferring one
nodes.rationale: Two independent reasons given: (1) Rufus-Air is proven at 106B-A12B with 27.04B SFT tokens on 512xH200, and the smallest published end-to-end SFT+RL pipeline anywhere is ~124M (nanochat), so dormouse today is 16x below that and its 100M-1B target lands in the one band actually run end to end; (2) the field moved past it in 2026 - INTELLECT-3, MiMo-V2.6 and Nemotron 3 collapsed serial per-domain RL into one mixed run plus multi-teacher on-policy distillation.

nodes.label: Post-training 2026 comparison report (2026-09-27)
nodes.rationale: Research report comparing 7 post-training recipes (Rufus-Air, Tulu 3, INTELLECT-3, MiMo-V2.6, Open-Reasoner-Zero, SimpleRL-Zoo, nanochat) plus ~30 small-scale papers, against dormouse: a 7.5M byte-level LM targeting 100M-1B. Every source was opened and read this session (per the report's own accounting).

nodes.label: ATOD arXiv 2606.27814 (small SLM agents: ALFWorld / WebShop / Search-QA)
nodes.norm_label: atod arxiv 2606.27814 (small slm agents: alfworld / webshop / search-qa)
nodes.rationale: The clearest small-scale verdict on GRPO for agentic work: ATOD beats OPD by 4.16 points and GRPO by 23.62 points, and beats its own teacher by 2.16. Stated reason is structural: RL optimizes reward but 'sparse and delayed feedback makes early-stage learning much less efficient than OPD.' Credit assignment over a long sparse horizon.

nodes.label: Auditing GRPO/SFT/DPO arXiv 2609.00925 (3B)
nodes.rationale: At 3B, GRPO variants produced SMALL grounding gains; conflict-SFT and DPO produced the gains, and after a supervised warm start the same GRPO recipe added essentially nothing further.

nodes.label: Bittensor Agent Arenas arXiv 2606.10064 (Qwen3-4B, ShoppingBench)
nodes.rationale: 'Small-model agentic post-training is bottlenecked less by the algorithm than by the trajectory substrate it consumes.' Frontier-synthesised data collapses the long tail; production logs are contaminated by shortcut behaviour. SFT leaves a big pass@8 -> pass@1 gap (53.3% vs 34.8%); a per-step teacher-grounded Dr. GRPO reward converts that headroom into process improvement.

nodes.label: ChemCRAFT arXiv 2601.17687 (SLM + sandbox)
nodes.rationale: 'Scientific reasoning is not solely an emergent ability of model scale, but a learnable policy of tool orchestration.' SMILES-GRPO for a dense chemical reward.

nodes.label: Domyn-Small 10B arXiv 2607.20448
nodes.rationale: GRPO-VR -> DPO -> a final multi-environment GRPO across five domains including tool calling. A serial-then-mixed hybrid; cited as evidence that the serial-vs-mixed question is unresolved.

nodes.label: DR-Venus arXiv 2604.19859 (4B)
nodes.rationale: ~10K open-data trajectories. Agentic SFT (strict cleaning + resampling of long-horizon trajectories) -> agentic RL on IGPO with TURN-LEVEL rewards based on information gain + format-aware regularization, explicitly 'to make RL effective for small agents.' Beats prior agentic models under 9B.

nodes.label: GRLO arXiv 2605.15464 (Qwen3-4B-Base)
nodes.rationale: The cheap path: RLHF learned FROM SCRATCH in open-ended environments with 5K prompts and 22.7 GPU-hours; 24.1 -> 63.1 average, ~46x less data and ~68x less compute than an in-domain RLVR baseline, competitive with Qwen's released post-trained models. A SUBSEQUENT in-domain RLVR stage 'brings only selective gains.'

nodes.label: GRPO for SLM function calling arXiv 2509.04518
nodes.norm_label: grpo for slm function calling arxiv 2509.04518
nodes.rationale: A well-shaped reward - structured-JSON validity + correct tool selection + precise parameter use - makes GRPO work for function calling at small scale.

nodes.label: INTELLECT-3 (Prime Intellect, 2025-11-26)
nodes.rationale: 2 stages: one large SFT on GLM-4.5-Air base -> one large-scale MIXED RL stage across Math, Code, Science, Logic, Deep Research, SWE. 512xH200 / 64 nodes / 2 months. All rewards rule-based/verifiable, no preference stage. Infrastructure-first: prime-rl is async-only ('the only practical way to scale RL to long-horizon agentic rollouts'), verifiers + Environments Hub (500+ tasks), Prime Sandboxes (direct Rust->pod, sub-10s startup, hundreds of sandboxes/node, provisioning overlapped with first-turn reasoning). Checkpoint is a budget checkpoint, not converged. Forward work: make the model manage its own context (cut/branch/external memory).

nodes.label: L20-Edu-135M arXiv 2606.22189
nodes.rationale: 134.5M, one L20. Direct GRPO-style RLVR on GSM8K DECREASED exact-match accuracy 1.82% -> 1.59% (192-token completions) and 1.21% (320-token). Authors are careful: 'these single-run results identify a concrete failure mode rather than establishing a general lower bound.' The closest published analogue to a 7.5M model with a sparse outcome reward and no format floor.

nodes.label: Learning from Less arXiv 2604.18381 (SLM, low-data RLVR)
nodes.norm_label: learning from less arxiv 2604.18381 (slm, low-data rlvr)
nodes.rationale: On procedural tasks, models trained on lower-complexity tasks generalize to higher complexity; mixed-complexity data gives up to 5x the sample efficiency of easy-only data.

nodes.label: RLVR for code (MBPP) arXiv 2605.30478
nodes.rationale: Qwen3-0.6B and Llama3.2-1B (LoRA), GRPO vs GSPO on MBPP. RLVR improves pass@1 by up to 13pp with a combined unit-test + linter reward. Hazard: static-analysis-only shaping biases the policy toward SHORTER completions that reduce lint errors without reliably improving functional correctness; combined rewards fix the degeneration.

nodes.label: MENTOR arXiv 2510.18383 (SLM, executable-tool benchmarks)
nodes.rationale: Names the small-model dilemma exactly: 'sparse outcome rewards provide insufficient guidance, whereas strict trajectory matching imposes overly restrictive constraints.' On-policy distillation with a flexible, process-aware reward beats both SFT and strict RL OOD.

nodes.label: MiMo-7B arXiv 2505.07608
nodes.rationale: Cited in the copy-from list for two things: test-difficulty-weighted dense code reward, and the thesis that RL pays only after the base is pretrained for the skill - dormouse's lever is the pretraining corpus first. Abstract only, not re-read this session.

nodes.label: MiMo-V2.6 (Xiaomi, ~2026-09)
nodes.rationale: Stages: cold start (incl. Aligned RL, cold-starting from the model's own self-correction) -> ONE mixed RL run -> MOPD2 multi-teacher on-policy distillation. 309B total / 15B active sparse MoE, 1M ctx, omni modal, 5-layer MTP drafter. 'You Only RL Once': coding, general agents, visual, cybersecurity from multiple harnesses in the same batch. Async GRPO, 1,568 prompts x 16 rollouts/step. Groupwise Agentic Grading: GRS builds task-specific rubrics offline from contrasting rollouts, GAR ranks passing trajectories toward higher-quality/shorter ones ('binary pass/fail cannot rank passing solutions'). Core thesis: scale the grader as the scarce resource once outcome reward saturates. Weights + dataset open, no training-code repo.

nodes.label: Nanbeige4.1-3B arXiv 2602.13367
nodes.rationale: A 3B generalist doing reasoning + code + agentic together: complexity-aware code rewards (correctness AND efficiency), and turn-level supervision in deep search giving reliable 600-tool-call turns.

nodes.label: nanochat Karpathy SFT+RL pipeline (github.com/karpathy/nanochat)
nodes.rationale: The only complete SFT+RL pipeline published at ~124M: d12 is GPT-1-sized (~124M) and the recommended iteration scale; d24 is GPT-2-grade (val_bpb 0.718, CORE 0.2690, beating GPT-2's 0.256525 in 1.80h on 8xH100). Whole ladder = three scripts (pretrain, chat_sft.py, chat_rl.py), read in full (README + both scripts + speedrun.sh). dormouse's target band 100M-1B lands exactly here, and dormouse today is 16x below it.

nodes.label: Nemotron-3-Nano-CC arXiv 2609.02849 (30B-A3B)
nodes.rationale: 22K curated problems, SFT + RL for competitive programming: IOI 2025 130 -> 291 post-training, 468 with GenCorrect test-time compute.

nodes.label: Nemotron 3 Ultra arXiv 2606.15007 (550B/55B)
nodes.rationale: SFT -> RL -> MOPD (multi-teacher on-policy distillation), multi-environment RLVR, NVFP4, reasoning budget control. Independent confirmation from a fourth org of the SFT -> mixed-RL -> OPD tail.

nodes.label: Nemotron IMO recipe arXiv 2609.10712
nodes.rationale: Listed under frontier confirmations in the report's source list; no per-paper numbers are recorded in the body, so the node is a citation anchor only.

nodes.label: Open-Reasoner-Zero arXiv 2503.24290 (StepFun/Tsinghua, 2025-03)
nodes.rationale: ONE stage: pure RL from base, no SFT at all, Qwen2.5-32B-Base. Vanilla PPO, GAE(lambda=1, gamma=1), NO KL regularization (KL and entropy coefficients zero). Beats DeepSeek-R1-Zero on AIME2024/MATH500/GPQA-Diamond at 1/10 the training steps. The learned critic devalues repetitive responses. Its result is minimalism: KL and a curated SFT floor are unnecessary for the reasoning-RL phenomenon at 32B. Doubles as the invitation to run an SFT->RLVR vs RLVR-from-base A/B.

nodes.label: Outcome rewards and causal reasoning arXiv 2604.22074
nodes.norm_label: outcome rewards and causal reasoning arxiv 2604.22074
nodes.rationale: Outcome rewards do not reliably make reasoning causally important or verifier-sufficient, and a SMALL AMOUNT of SFT before RLVR is the documented remedy. The counterweight to the two audits that undercut the SFT floor.

nodes.label: Plasticity vs Rigidity arXiv 2601.06677 (<=1.5B, one A40, <24h, RLVR+LoRA)
nodes.norm_label: plasticity vs rigidity arxiv 2601.06677 (<=1.5b, one a40, <24h, rlvr+lora)
nodes.rationale: LoRA r=8 consistently fails; r=256 unlocks plasticity -> 40.0% pass@1 on AIME 24 (+11.1 abs), pass@16 70.0%. But heavily math-aligned models suffered performance COLLAPSE: 'noisy, low-budget RL updates can act as destructive interference for models already residing near a task-specific optimum.' Instruction-tuned models instead spent the budget elongating CoT to maximize reward.

nodes.label: Prefix-GRPO arXiv 2607.19395 (TextCraft / BabyAI / ALFWorld)
nodes.rationale: 'Direct distillation from strong teacher trajectories often turns rich multi-turn behavior into one-shot imitation targets,' which is inefficient in long-horizon environments. Replay teacher prefixes to recover valid intermediate states, then let the student continue online; ablations show replay alone is insufficient without explicit prefix-token optimization.

nodes.label: Puro-2B arXiv 2608.27370 (1.5B, $6.9K pretraining)
nodes.rationale: Cheap pretraining recipe whose unusual value here is an end-to-end case study of how pretraining data curricula shape post-training outcomes - only possible because the full pipeline is published.

nodes.label: Reward granularity in RLVR arXiv 2607.02869 (Qwen2.5-0.5B, GRPO, GSM8K)
nodes.norm_label: reward granularity in rlvr arxiv 2607.02869 (qwen2.5-0.5b, grpo, gsm8k)
nodes.rationale: Process-only 63.73% vs outcome-only 53.75% - a ~10pp gap at 0.5B. Process models produce structurally consistent, arithmetically grounded traces; outcome models produce concise but derivation-error-prone chains. Hybrid weights track the process weight EXCEPT lambda=0.1 (low process / high outcome), which underperforms pure outcome - conflicting signals.

nodes.label: Rufus-Air arXiv 2609.29421 (Amazon, 2026-09-24)
nodes.rationale: GLM-4.5-Air-Base 106B-A12B MoE. 8 serial stages: SFT -> Reasoning RL -> Coding RL -> IF RL -> General Agent -> Coding Agent -> Search Agent -> RLHF. SFT 9.01M samples / 44.5B raw tokens / 27.04B loss-bearing tokens, 17 public datasets, zero regenerated, zero human annotation; Math+Coding Agent = 18.8% of samples but 49.1% of training tokens; decontamination removed 4,187 unique samples. SFT ckpt 3799 alone beats the official RL-included release (IFEval +5.3, IFBench +24.2, AIME25 +6.6, AIME26 +3.5, GPQA -5.7). DAPO 4x oversample, groups with mean reward in (0,0.8]. Sandbox fleet ~10K concurrent = $10K/month. Self-declared limits in §6: stage order 'worked, not shown optimal', Coding Agent not to convergence, no cross-stage benchmark, no multi-teacher OPD. No dedicated code repo.

nodes.label: Salesforce Koa arXiv 2609.15066 (Nemotron-3-Super-120B base)
nodes.rationale: Spec-driven GRPO: expand workflow specs into persona-conditioned multi-turn tasks with task-resolution rewards grounded in successful tool use. Gains clearest on multi-turn tool use.

nodes.label: SEA-LION v4.8 arXiv 2609.18310 (SFT + online OPD)
nodes.rationale: Listed under frontier confirmations; a fifth org's SFT-then-OPD shape. No numbers in the report body - citation anchor only.

nodes.label: Selective Left-Shift arXiv 2607.07748 (SLM code, Qwen3-8B main runs)
nodes.norm_label: selective left-shift arxiv 2607.07748 (slm code, qwen3-8b main runs)
nodes.rationale: States the trilemma plainly: SFT is bottlenecked by data scarcity, test-time scaling too expensive, and 'Reinforcement Learning from scratch yields near zero advantages.' Pipeline: offline synthesis with iterative compiler+test feedback -> SFT on verified data -> RLVR on execution-grounded I/O tests, 'where the SFT prior constrains exploration away from syntax errors.' Ablations confirm BOTH the SFT phase and execution-grounded rewards are necessary for stable training.

nodes.label: SimpleRL-Zoo arXiv 2503.18892 (HKUST, COLM 2025)
nodes.rationale: ONE stage, zero RL with rule-based math rewards, from base, across 10 base models Qwen2.5 0.5B-32B plus Llama3-8B, Mistral-7B/24B, DeepSeek-Math-7B, Qwen2.5-math-7B. The only one of the six with sub-1B evidence. Mostly negative results: 'we find the base models already exhibit strong instruction-following and self-reflection abilities', so Qwen-focused reproductions overstate generality. The aha moment was FIRST observed in non-Qwen small models and only with format-reward adjustment and query-difficulty control. Increased response length does not always correlate with verification behaviour.

nodes.label: SmolLM3 (HF blog, 3B fully-open recipe)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately skips RL ('most existing approaches involve complex RL processes and proprietary datasets'). Shape: reasoning MID-TRAINING (35B-token dataset, 4 epochs ~ 140B tokens, ChatML, wrapped packing) -> SFT 1.8B tokens (1B non-reasoning + 0.8B reasoning, 4 epochs, BFD packing, loss masked on user turns AND tool results) -> APO off-policy DPO (Tulu 3 preference mixture for non-reasoning; synthetic reasoning pairs with Qwen3-32B chosen, Qwen3-0.6B rejected) -> model merge 0.9 APO-soup / 0.1 mid-training checkpoint, which recovered the RULER score APO had destroyed. Chat template separates XML Tools from Python Tools sections; /think vs /no_think are system-prompt flags with pre-filled empty think blocks.

nodes.label: SmolTulu arXiv 2412.08347
nodes.rationale: Tulu 3 pipeline (SFT -> DPO, NO RLVR) at SmolLM2-1.7B -> SOTA sub-2B: IFEval 67.7 (+11), GSM8K 51.6 (+3.4), ARC variant 57.1 (+5.4). Ablations at 135M. The methodologically load-bearing finding: the LR-to-batch-size ratio is strongly task-dependent - reasoning tasks (ARC, GSM8K) want higher ratios, pattern-recognition tasks (HellaSwag, IFEval) want lower. Recipe hyperparameters do not transfer down-scale even when the stage structure does.

nodes.label: SOD step-wise on-policy distillation arXiv 2605.07725
nodes.rationale: 0.6B student, 26.13% on AIME 2025 via tool-integrated reasoning. Names the OPD failure mode: erroneous tool calls cascade across subsequent steps, progressively amplifying student-teacher divergence until the teacher's token supervision is useless. Step-wise divergence reweighting fixes it, up to +20.86% over the second-best baseline.

nodes.label: Stage-1 controls entropy, not outcome arXiv 2606.09059
nodes.norm_label: stage-1 controls entropy, not outcome arxiv 2606.09059
nodes.rationale: Matched small-data study: three warm-starts (SFT, OPD, ...) landed in a narrow 53-54% band in-domain. What Stage 1 actually controlled was the ENTROPY REGIME entering RL, not the endpoint.

nodes.label: SWE-Protégé arXiv 2602.22124 (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct)
nodes.rationale: States the SLM SWE failure mode bluntly: 'pervasive action looping and low resolution rates.' Fix = learn to selectively consult an expert, recognize stalled states, follow through; SFT on expert-augmented trajectories + agentic RL that EXPLICITLY PENALIZES degenerate looping and unproductive expert collaboration -> 42.4% SWE-bench Verified (+25.4) with ~4 expert calls/task and 11% of tokens.

nodes.label: Terminus-4B arXiv 2605.03195 (Qwen3-4B post-trained)
nodes.rationale: A 4B subagent (SFT + RL with rubric-based LLM-judge reward) for terminal execution cuts the main agent's token usage ~30% at no performance cost, and beats Claude Sonnet / Opus / GPT-5.3-Codex on that subtask.

nodes.label: TinyLLM arXiv 2511.22138 (TinyAgent, TinyLlama, Qwen, xLAM, BFCL)
nodes.norm_label: tinyllm arxiv 2511.22138 (tinyagent, tinyllama, qwen, xlam, bfcl)
nodes.rationale: 1-3B models significantly outperform <1B models on function calling; best 65.74% overall and 55.62% multi-turn with a hybrid SFT+PEFT+RL+DPO recipe. Direct evidence that <1B tool-calling is a weak regime.

nodes.label: Replacing thinking with tool usage arXiv 2507.05065 (DeepMind, up to 3B)
nodes.norm_label: replacing thinking with tool usage arxiv 2507.05065 (deepmind, up to 3b)
nodes.rationale: Instead of spending test compute on natural-language CoT, format those tokens as a multi-turn interaction trace with a stateful tool in a custom DSL. Yields faster sampling and a denser reward signal - 'allowing even models of size up to 3B parameters to learn how to proficiently expend additional compute.'

nodes.label: Tulu 3 arXiv 2411.15124 (AI2, 2024-11, v5 2025-04)
nodes.rationale: 3 stages SFT -> DPO -> RLVR (RLVR last), PPO with rule-based rewards on GSM8K/MATH/IFEval. Llama 3.1 8B/70B/405B; smallest proven 8B. Coined RLVR as a named method; multi-task eval with development and unseen splits, decontamination, full data+code+infra release, and explicit publication of training methods that did NOT reliably improve performance (online DPO, rejection sampling). Data findings: scaling unique prompts beats reusing SFT prompts; on-policy pairs beat off-policy.

nodes.label: ufakzeka-1 arXiv 2609.25081 (151M / 182M w/ embeddings)
nodes.rationale: ~$286, byte-level TOKENIZER at 1.77 tok/word, three-stage pretrain then post-training on open + generated data, NO RL. The nearest byte-level data point in the literature. Three transferable findings: (a) a safety gate 'fixed' with data written from its own questions read 64/64 when the honest figure was 34/64; (b) training-seed variance was as large as the spread across EVERY recipe tried, so single-seed comparisons at this scale are uninformative; (c) data rounds repaired only what was absent - identity tracking over long context and multi-turn arithmetic did not move under any data change, 'which we read as limits of the model size rather than gaps in the data'.

nodes.label: dormouse-specific risk: the Engram creates a task-specific optimum on memorization
nodes.norm_label: dormouse-specific risk: the engram creates a task-specific optimum on memorization
nodes.rationale: No published small-model RL result has an analogue: an in-model n-gram memory table means the model is already near-optimal on memorization (dormouse's Engram drives train CE to ~0 while held-out stays hard), and 2601.06677 documents exactly that regime - a model near a task-specific optimum - producing collapse under noisy low-budget RL. Prescribed instrumentation: watch train-vs-held-out SEPARATION during Stage 1, not just the reward curve.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: eval integrity fails silently at small scale (64/64 read, 34/64 true)
nodes.norm_label: negative: eval integrity fails silently at small scale (64/64 read, 34/64 true)
nodes.rationale: Measured: ufakzeka-1's safety gate, 'fixed' with data written from its own questions, read 64/64 when the honest figure was 34/64 - the eval data had leaked into the fix. The report maps this to dormouse's own history: train-CE collapse from a 24M-row n-gram memorizer while held-out stayed at 5.5, the same failure mode in a different place. Rule: hold out eval bytes BEFORE building any post-training data; decontamination must be a script that runs before every build, not a manual pass.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: format reward is a per-base knob, and Qwen bases self-reflect before RL
nodes.norm_label: negative: format reward is a per-base knob, and qwen bases self-reflect before rl
nodes.rationale: Measured across 10 base models in SimpleRL-Zoo: 'we find the base models already exhibit strong instruction-following and self-reflection abilities' and the aha moment was FIRST observed in non-Qwen small models, only with careful format-reward adjustment and query-difficulty control. Consequence for dormouse: it is a from-scratch non-Qwen base, so assume format reward needs its own sweep and do NOT read any Qwen-0.5B result as a prior.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: GRPO is the wrong algorithm for small multi-turn agents
nodes.norm_label: negative: grpo is the wrong algorithm for small multi-turn agents
nodes.rationale: Measured: ATOD on small SLM agents over ALFWorld / WebShop / Search-QA - ATOD beats OPD by 4.16 points and GRPO by 23.62 points, and beats its own teacher by 2.16. Stated mechanism: credit assignment over a long sparse horizon; 'sparse and delayed feedback makes early-stage learning much less efficient than OPD.' Corroborated by MENTOR (sparse outcome rewards give insufficient guidance; strict trajectory matching over-constrains) and Prefix-GRPO (direct distillation turns multi-turn behaviour into one-shot imitation targets).

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: recipe hyperparameters do not transfer down-scale even when the stage structure does
nodes.norm_label: negative: recipe hyperparameters do not transfer down-scale even when the stage structure does
nodes.rationale: Measured: SmolTulu ablations at 135M (model at 1.7B) - the LR-to-batch-size ratio is strongly task-dependent. Reasoning tasks (ARC, GSM8K) want HIGHER ratios; pattern-recognition tasks (HellaSwag, IFEval) want LOWER. Consequence: dormouse must re-tune the ratio per task family rather than inheriting nanochat's numbers wholesale; only the stage structure is claimed to transfer.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: response length growth is not capability growth
nodes.norm_label: negative: response length growth is not capability growth
nodes.rationale: Measured: SimpleRL-Zoo across 0.5B-32B - increased response length does not always correlate with the emergence of verification behaviour (the 'aha moment'). The same paper notes instruction-tuned models at small scale spent the RL budget elongating CoT to maximize reward. Operational rule: track a capability metric (ChatCORE-style), not response length.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: static-analysis-only reward shaping degenerates at small scale
nodes.norm_label: negative: static-analysis-only reward shaping degenerates at small scale
nodes.rationale: Measured: Qwen3-0.6B / Llama3.2-1B LoRA on MBPP. Linter-only shaping biases the policy toward shorter completions that reduce lint errors WITHOUT reliably improving functional correctness. The fix is a combined unit-test + linter reward, which is also the configuration that yields the up-to-13pp pass@1 gain. Directly rules out 'cheap partial verifiers' as a shortcut reward for dormouse Stage 1.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: on-policy distillation has its own small-model failure mode (tool-call cascade)
nodes.norm_label: negative: on-policy distillation has its own small-model failure mode (tool-call cascade)
nodes.rationale: Measured: SOD, 0.6B student. Erroneous tool calls cascade across subsequent steps, progressively amplifying student-teacher divergence until the teacher's token-level supervision is actively misleading. Fix = step-wise divergence reweighting, worth up to +20.86% over the second-best baseline, and the same fix path yields 26.13% on AIME 2025. So the OPD recommendation carries a named, cheap mitigation.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: plain GRPO with a sparse outcome reward made a 135M model worse
nodes.norm_label: negative: plain grpo with a sparse outcome reward made a 135m model worse
nodes.rationale: Measured: L20-Edu-135M (134.5M, one L20), direct GRPO-style RLVR on GSM8K, GSM8K exact-match accuracy 1.82% -> 1.59% at 192-token completions and 1.21% at 320 tokens. Against: the same task with an SFT format floor. Authors explicitly label it a failure-mode demonstration, not a bound. Why it matters for dormouse: it is the closest published analogue to '7.5M model, sparse outcome reward, no format floor'.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: named small-model RL techniques that fail outright (LoRA r=8, GRPO multi-turn, prefix replay alone)
nodes.norm_label: negative: named small-model rl techniques that fail outright (lora r=8, grpo multi-turn, prefix replay alone)
nodes.rationale: Three named small-model traps. (a) LoRA r=8 consistently fails for RL plasticity at <=1.5B where r=256 succeeds (2601.06677). (b) GRPO for multi-turn agents loses to distillation by 23.62 points (2606.27814). (c) Prefix replay alone is insufficient without explicit prefix-token optimization (2607.19395). The transferable positive from the same cluster: mixed-complexity data gives up to 5x the sample efficiency of easy-only data (2604.18381), and execution-grounded rewards plus an SFT prior are jointly necessary for stable RLVR (2607.07748).

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: noisy low-budget RL collapses models already near a task-specific optimum
nodes.norm_label: negative: noisy low-budget rl collapses models already near a task-specific optimum
nodes.rationale: Measured: at <=1.5B on one A40 in <24h with RLVR + LoRA, heavily math-aligned models suffered performance COLLAPSE while instruction-tuned models merely elongated CoT to farm reward. Quoted mechanism: 'noisy, low-budget RL updates can act as destructive interference for models already residing near a task-specific optimum.' (Same paper: LoRA r=8 consistently fails, r=256 unlocks plasticity -> 40.0% pass@1 AIME24, +11.1 abs, pass@16 70.0%.) Dormouse-specific angle: its Engram already drives train CE to ~0 while held-out stays hard - a near-optimum on a memorization task, which is exactly the regime that collapsed.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: two audits say the SFT floor may be less load-bearing than the doctrine claims
nodes.norm_label: negative: two audits say the sft floor may be less load-bearing than the doctrine claims
nodes.rationale: Two independent measurements. (a) At 3B (2609.00925), GRPO variants produced SMALL grounding gains while conflict-SFT and DPO produced the gains, and after a supervised warm start the same GRPO recipe added essentially nothing further. (b) In a matched small-data study (2606.09059) three warm-starts landed in a narrow 53-54% band in-domain; what Stage 1 actually controlled was the entropy regime entering RL, not the endpoint. Counterweight (2604.22074): outcome rewards do not reliably make reasoning causally important or verifier-sufficient, and a small amount of SFT before RLVR is the documented remedy. Net: keep Stage 0, budget one cheap A/B (SFT->RLVR vs RLVR-from-base) once Stage 1 exists, exactly as ORZ's result invites.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: single-seed A/Bs at this scale measure nothing
nodes.norm_label: negative: single-seed a/bs at this scale measure nothing
nodes.rationale: Measured: ufakzeka-1 at 151M - 'training-seed variance was as large as the spread across every recipe tried', so single-seed comparisons at this scale are uninformative. Direct instruction: dormouse A/Bs need >=3 seeds per arm before concluding anything, applied to both the recipe A/Bs and the SFT->RLVR vs RLVR-from-base test.

nodes.label: NEGATIVE: SLM agents loop - pervasive action looping and low resolution rates
nodes.norm_label: negative: slm agents loop - pervasive action looping and low resolution rates
nodes.rationale: Measured: SWE-Protégé on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, SWE-bench Verified. Quoted failure: 'pervasive action looping and low resolution rates.' Fix = SFT on expert-augmented trajectories plus agentic RL that explicitly penalizes degenerate looping AND unproductive expert collaboration -> 42.4% (+25.4) with ~4 expert calls/task and 11% of tokens. Report notes this is consistent with dormouse having already deleted PonderNet (ADR-0013).

nodes.norm_label: loop runs at fixed max_iter=4 with honest unweighted ce

nodes.norm_label: the kl direction was wrong: p||prior makes collapse free
nodes.rationale: p*log(p/prior) -> 0 as p -> 0. Fixed to prior-weighted KL in the predecessor analysis and the collapse STILL won at practical beta: silencing the halt saves rec ~5.5 while beta*KL costs ~0.03.

nodes.label: lambda-collapse makes the PonderNet rec loss fake
nodes.norm_label: lambda-collapse makes the pondernet rec loss fake
nodes.rationale: 2026-09-25 official v2.1-era run: lambda -> 0 early, p_dist -> [9e-4, 4e-6, 1e-8, 2e-11]; rec = sum p*CE -> 0.005 was a FAKE loss (predictions garbage, weighted by ~0), out_acc -> 0, held-out eval froze at EXACTLY uniform (BPB 8.000 = ln256/ln2), generation emitted noise. RecurTrace (2609.03379) replicates it: ACT and PonderNet collapse to 1.0 loop at every regularization in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1}.

nodes.rationale: MobileLLM's deep-thin architectures plus embedding sharing plus GQA give +2.7%/+4.3% at 125M/350M, with immediate block-wise weight sharing adding +0.7%/+0.8% at near-zero latency (arXiv:2402.14905). Relaxed Recursive Transformers convert existing models to shared-layer recursion with layer-wise LoRA restoration (arXiv:2410.20672). Weight tying is a real but small-model-sized decision; at vocab 256 the head is only 256*d params, so decide by loss, not bytes (arXiv:1608.05859).

nodes.label: burn-muon-plus Muon+ optimizer for Burn
nodes.rationale: Claims Muon with one post-polar normalization step and zero extra optimizer state: M_t = mu*M_{t-1} + (1-mu)*G_t, O_t = Norm_d(Ortho(M_t)) (NS polar + row/col normalization), W_t = W_{t-1} - eta*sqrt(m/n)*O_t. Exports Norm_col, Norm_row and the sequential ColRow / RowCol compositions ('best in the paper'). Restates the paper's results: up to 37.1% pre-training speedup to a target loss, validation perplexity down by up to 2.02, works on top of any polar method (Jordan / You / PolarExpress / exact SVD); the paper's recipe is 2D weights on Muon+ and non-matrix parameters (biases, norms) falling back to AdamW. Claims fused cubecl kernels (NS polynomial combine, momentum, final decay+update, ColRow normalize with in-kernel reductions) collapsing ~45 elementwise tensor passes per step into a handful of launches: 22.4 ms -> 232 us (96x) on [4096x4096] and 47.3 ms -> 563 us (84x) on [8192x1024] on RTX 5060 Ti. Also claims the Newton-Schulz polynomial evaluated factored (a*x + b*(xx*x) + c*(xx*(xx*x))) is 3.6x faster on [8192,512] with a lower peak footprint and never materializes (XX^T)^2. All kernels verified == tensor path (<1e-4).

nodes.label: burn-sct Spectral Compact Training
nodes.rationale: Claims a drop-in nn.Linear replacement with weights stored as a permanent truncated SVD W = U*diag(s)*V^T, the dense matrix never materialized, the forward being three small matmuls O(b*k*(m+n)) instead of O(b*m*n). After each optimizer step U and V are retracted to the Stiefel manifold by QR retraction (paper Eq 5): Q, R = QR(M); M <- Q*sign(diag(R)), matching the paper's safe_qr. Claims up to 199x memory reduction per MLP layer at rank 32 including Adam states (LLaMA-70B 3758 MB -> 18.9 MB, 93x at 7B, 51x at 1.7B, 13x at 135M). The QR is the Householder decomposition adapted from burn-rs/burn (crates/burn-tensor/src/tensor/linalg/qr.rs, MIT), reduced to O(m*k^2) for the tall-skinny factors (m >> k) with reflection vectors stored in the R pass and Q built back-to-front (LAPACK orgqr scheme) so no m x m intermediate is ever materialized. Claims custom CUDA sct_qr_r/sct_qr_q kernels with no host round-trip (verified 2e-7) and an AVX2/FMA SIMD dot3 CPU fallback on x86_64. Claims bit-exactness against the official PyTorch reference EctoSpace/SCT: forward ~2e-7, retract ~1e-7, from_dense <= 5.9e-4 (one-sided Hestenes Jacobi, tolerance 1e-3), comparing rank-k reconstructions (sign-invariant) and never raw singular vectors. Forward is claimed memory-optimal (peak footprint is just the input plus the two GEMM outputs).

Base scaling base' = base * yarn_factor^(d/(d-2)); yarn_factor = 1.0 gives standard RoPE, > 1.0 extends context. Performance claim (RTX 3090, CUDA): the rotation (x1*c - x2*s, x1*s + x2*c) is a single elementwise launch per row instead of 4 muls + 2 adds + a [..., hd] cat, 22.4 ms -> 14.7 ms (1.5x) at b=4, t=2048, nh=32, hd=128. Inference: forward-only builds call the bare CUDA fused kernel directly, reusing precomputed cos/sin tables across calls.

nodes.label: burn-situ SiTU-GLU activation
nodes.rationale: Claims a 'Sigmoid-Tanh Unit (SiTU) gated linear activation' -- a bounded GLU variant from Kimi K3 -- applying softcap(x, beta) = beta*tanh(x/beta) to the gate and up branches, claimed to prevent activation explosion in deep models and to give MXFP4 quantization stability. Fused dispatch requires H % 8 == 0 (cubecl CUDA codegen corrupts coalesced stores on row strides that are not 32-byte multiples); other shapes fall back to the tensor path.
